 Judgment

Learned counsel for the appellants submits that as per the Valuation Slip filed before the Trial Court, the value of the subject matter of the present appeal is Rs.9,43,855/-, which is lesser than NC: 2023:KHC:39937 the upper pecuniary limit of Rs.10,00,000/- as contemplated under Section 19 of the Karnataka Civil Courts Act, 1964.

It is submitted that the appeal may be dismissed as withdrawn reserving liberty in favour of the appellants to approach the jurisdictional Appellate Smt. Thimmamma vs Smt. Sannamma on 8 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170211597/
3 Court.

It is also submitted that there was an interim order in the suit before the Trial Court, which restrains the defendant No.4 - respondent No.3 from receiving the compensation amount from respondent No.10 - SLAO in respect of the schedule 'D' property and the same may be continued for a period of 10 days so as to enable the appellants to approach the appropriate jurisdictional Appellate Court.
2.
The said submission is placed on record.
3. Per contra, learned counsel for caveator - respondent No.3 would oppose the said submission.
4. A perusal of the Valuation Slip filed by the appellants - plaintiffs will indicate that the value of the subject matter of the appeal is Rs.9,43,855/-.
Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed as withdrawn reserving liberty in favour of the appellants to approach the jurisdictional Appellate Court on or before 18.11.2023.

If such an appeal is preferred before the jurisdictional Appellate Court on or before 18.11.2023,
the appellants would be entitled to the benefit of Section 14 of the Limitation Act.

6. Further, in order to enable the appellants to approach the jurisdictional Appellate Court as stated supra, without prejudice to the rights and contentions of the parties and making it clear that the jurisdictional District Court shall hear both sides and pass appropriate orders, in accordance with law, without being influenced by the present order, I deem it just and appropriate to direct the respondent No.10 not to disburse the compensation amount in relation to item No.4 of the suit schedule properties, in favour of respondent No.3 till 18.11.2023.
7. All rival contentions on all aspects of the matter are kept open and no opinion is expressed on the same.
8. Registry is directed to return all the papers back to the appellants forthwith, without any further delay.

Sd/-
